parts.text: Which claim correctly explains how that food reached those parts?

options.text: Food made in the leaves reaches storage and growing parts through phloem.
Food made in the leaves reaches storage and growing parts through xylem.
Roots make the plant's food and send it through phloem to the leaves.
Starch in a potato proves the food was made inside the potato.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Zayd knows leaves make food by photosynthesis. A growing tip and a potato later show stored starch that was not made in those parts themselves.

part_answers.answer: Leaves make food; phloem carries that food to other parts. Xylem carries water and minerals, and starch stored in a potato was transported there, not made there.

teacher.key_rationale: Food made in leaves moves through phloem to storage and growing parts. Swapping in xylem, reversing roots as the food makers, or treating potato starch as proof of local manufacture miss that hinge.
